title: Model invariants and operation failure boundaries
description: Terms for model configuration, typed failure outcomes and the state preserved at each tested operation boundary.

terms.definition: Work around the decoder, such as reading native settings or publishing a checkpoint. The model validation, attention, gradient and optimizer decisions remain in the existing course operations.

A condition the existing decoder validator requires, such as a positive query-head count and residual width divisible by that count. Readable settings alone do not establish a valid or executable model.

The continuation rule attached to a typed failure: reject unchanged, discard provisional work, or stop the affected session or job. Its state promise applies at the declared operation boundary, not to every earlier successful update.

The explicit outcome of a failed operation: rejected, failed, cancelled or timed out. It is recorded separately from the reason and disposition; a later cancellation does not retract an already committed result.

Candidate output or owned payload that has not crossed its commit point. The local harness can discard it while retaining committed counters; failed cleanup instead reports retained ownership and forbids reuse.

Separate bindings for the configuration requested and the implementation actually selected. Before selection, actual identity remains not_selected; an available substitute does not silently become the requested backend.
